sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Posterior part of the head pale yellow, becoming reddish brown anteriorly; postclypeus reddish brown; brown below and in front of the antennal sockets; anteclypeus pale yellow with white patches; labrum brownish yellow, apex white; mandibles dark reddish brown, paler at the base; antennae brownish yellow; pronotum pale yellow with light brown patches; tergites and sternites creamy yellow; legs pale yellow. Head with a few scattered stiff setae, frontal projection with 2–3 moderately long stiff setae; pronotum sparsely provided with a few setae; longitudinal ridge of the fore coxa with 1 long seta and several short hairs. Head wide and thick; posterior margin broadly rounded; frontal projection distinct, its anterior margin rounded in lateral view; frons inclined about 55° towards the anteclypeus; frontoclypeal region weakly concave. Mandibles short and stout, outer margin of the base concave, bending strongly from the notch towards the apex; lower half of the left mandible with four notches. Postmental constriction index 0.54–0.55. Antennae 13-segmented; segment 2 longer than segment 3, segment 4 the shortest. Anterior margin of the pronotum distinctly concave in the middle, posterior margin notched. Measurements (2 soldiers, in mm; holotype / paratype, as in the OCR): head length (to mandible base) "25/2.25"; head width "80/1.78"; head height "50/1.50"; left mandible length "84/0.84"; postmentum greatest width "—/0.56"; postmentum least width "30/0.31"; postmentum length "46/1.43"; pronotum greatest length "66/0.60"; pronotum width "09/1.09"; hind tibia length "43/1.43".

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is closest to F. coatoni, from which it differs in the wider head, the more narrowly rounded posterior lateral corners of the head, the stronger median constriction of the postmentum, and the stouter mandibles, whose outer margin curves more strongly from the notch towards the apex.

note: Rewritten from Krishna 1963. This window (_tmp/ia_pack6/foraminitermes-harrisi.txt) does not contain the morphological description: the descriptive text is in the adjacent window _tmp/ia_pack6/foraminitermes-coatoni.txt, lines 193–210, and the comparison sentence at lines 212–230; this window supplies the comparison, the type locality and TABLE 4. In TABLE 4 the OCR has lost the leading digit in many places ("25", "80", "50", "84", "30", "46", "66", "09", "43"; for postmentum greatest width only the paratype value 0.56 survives); the holotype column is incomplete and is reproduced without restoration. OCR misread harrisi as "harrist". Type locality: Keyberg, 10 km south of Elisabethville (Congo), collected by Emerson on 1948-04-17 in underground tunnels in grassland.
